name: Lauterbrunnen Village Floor
tagline: The valley hub beneath the Staubbach Falls
description: The main village on the flat valley floor, home to the railway station, shops, hotels, and most services. It is the transport gateway to every upper village and sits directly under the Staubbach Falls, offering the easiest access and the widest choice of accommodation.
bestFor: First-timers and remote workers wanting services and easy transport
pros: Best transport links and station access
Most shops, hotels, and grocery options
cons: Busiest and most touristy part of the valley
Less peaceful than the car-free upper villages

name: Wengen
tagline: Car-free sun terrace on the eastern shelf
description: A car-free village perched on a sunny shelf high above the valley's eastern side, reached by cog railway. Wengen offers sweeping Jungfrau views, gentle alpine charm, and direct access to hiking and skiing, with a calmer, more resort-like feel than the valley floor.
bestFor: Slow travellers wanting quiet, sun, and big views

name: Murren
tagline: Cliff-edge car-free village under the Schilthorn
description: A tiny car-free village clinging to the western cliff, reached by cable car and mountain railway. Murren sits beneath the Schilthorn with dramatic views across to the Eiger, Monch, and Jungfrau. It is serene, high, and a favourite of hikers and skiers seeking altitude and calm.
bestFor: Hikers and quiet-seekers who love altitude
cons: Multi-stage access by cable car and rail

name: Gimmelwald
tagline: Sleepy car-free hamlet on the western slope
description: A minuscule car-free farming hamlet below Murren on the western slope, reached by cable car from Stechelberg. Gimmelwald is quiet, rustic, and beloved by budget-minded hikers for its hostel and unspoiled character, offering the most authentic and low-key stay in the whole valley.
bestFor: Hikers wanting the quietest, most authentic base
